verification: CI fixtures: two named brains, personal and swarm, holding an arc with the same key and the same project. Embeddings cases run against the CI pgvector server with two login principals mul04_personal and mul04_swarm, each owning one schema. Vaults are distinct scratch directories under a fake HOME. Redis is a dict backed fake in brain-ops tests (mocked); CLI compose and docker calls are faked. No deployed brain was contacted.
state: observed in CI; Redis and docker mocked, Postgres real
assertions: Two brains on one Postgres server through distinct principals and schemas store the same arc key and project; a search by the swarm brain returns only swarm knowledge and the personal schema still holds only personal knowledge and its claim.
A principal cannot read the other brain's schema (InsufficientPrivilege).
Distinct principals, schemas, vaults and namespaced Redis keys report no scope conflict; installed brains with distinct backends report none.
Named brains announce ticks on brain:<id>:events:brain and read with consumer group brain:<id>:amygdala; the default brain keeps legacy keys.
brain-api claims an unclaimed vault at startup; the claim file is not served by /vault/list.
Every migration receives the brain id and the brain_instance claim migration runs.
